Well, you have to root your phone in order to install a new ROM, so you can root it without having a new ROM. I am currently doing just that on my S4.

Also, if the new ROM you want to flash runs Lollipop, there is an option to import a list of all the apps you had downloaded the last time the Play Store updated your file in the clouds, and it will install them as part of the setup process. Settings you will have to change though.

Installing a new ROM is like going from Windows 8 to Windows 7, they are both the same operating system, but they are set up differently. They can have differing UIs, can have a lot of the privately apps that are considered bloat removed and can have scripts that allow the processor and programs to function more efficiently.

Yes, you can root your phone without installing a new ROM. I root primarly because I bought and paid for the device and I should have total control over it. For me it's like buying a computer but not having administrator access to anything. Each rooting method is different per device because of the hardware and all the software modifications carriers do with their phones.  

A good benefit is for ad blocking and for removing carrier bloatware. Yes, you can disable apps that came with the phone, but personally I'd rather get those completely removed since I'd never use them. I bought a phone last year and the stuff that came with it out of the box was basically garbage. I have no use for an antivirus app on my phone, nor do I want 3 different forms of address book services, and I really don't want facebook installed on my phone.

Yes, you can root your phone without installing a new ROM.

That's good news.

You can get rid of all the crapware that is bundled with your phone by default. Asides from that I've never really bothered with any other functionalities, although it does let you install custom ROMs.

1. I think that I should have root on every device I own. I paid for it, after all.
  2. AdAway. When I first got a smartphone, the thing that amazed me was the volume of ads on it. Every app comes with a shit-ton of ads. There is an ad blocker, AdAway, but in order to use it you have to root your phone.
  3. ROMs. These are basically alternate OSes for your phone. They're all hacked variants of the Android OS, but they've got some cool features that the stock OS doesn't have.
  4. Remove bloatware. There are always "important" programs that your provider wants you to have on your phone. They don't provide any essential functions, but you can't uninstall them unless you're rooted.

I'll add that rooting isn't complicated at all. It's actually a very simple process.
For nexus devices you can just plug it in and use Nexus Root Toolkit, does it get more complicated for other brands?
